description: Normalized calculator inputs for the golden set: the 'extraction answer key'. Values are taken from data/golden_set/<case_id>.json. Units: LDL-C and non-HDL-C in mmol/L, apoB and Lp(a) in mg/dL. Changes are placebo-adjusted; negative = reduction.

cases.input_notes: apoB -15% / -12 mg/dL is from Ference 2017 (verified_primary=false).
Lipid changes from phase 2 dal-VESSEL (phase 3 paper reports only 'minimal effect' on LDL).
Niacin target (HCAR2) genetics not established -> uncertain. One-sided 0.025 = two-sided 0.05.
LDL abs = study-average difference; pct values are weeks 12-24.
sPLA2 change from phase 2 (phase 3 value not found). LDL baseline not given.
Lp(a) baseline not given -> Lp(a) term skipped (no default baseline for Lp(a)).
LDL at month 12 (ITT): -48.4 mg/dL.
LDL = time-averaged difference over the trial (-22 mg/dL).
150 mg arm vs placebo.
FRESH. -80% is the design-paper projection (not measured). Follow-up unknown (>=2.5 y): 3.0 assumed. Events = planned. Outcome numbers not disclosed.
Sensitivity variant: -72% (press figure / phase 2 60 mg arm).
Baseline 260.3 nmol/L converted with 2.4 nmol/L per mg/dL (assumption; no fixed conversion exists). Planned events not public.
Baseline 253.9 nmol/L converted with 2.4 nmol/L per mg/dL (assumption). Planned events not public.

LDL-C at 14 weeks (placebo-adjusted -56.8%; absolute -73.8 mg/dL = -1.908 mmol/L from registry LS mean difference). Attenuated to -43.2% at 52 weeks (antidrug antibodies), so the time-averaged effect is smaller. Median follow-up 12 months (trial stopped early by sponsor). Events = 179 + 224 primary events. Lp(a) baseline 19.1 mg/dL median not used (Lp(a) term skipped as in fourier).

LDL-C/apoB increased (positive = rise). LDL-C abs +0.26 mmol/L and apoB abs +5 mg/dL from Doi 2024 (verified_primary=false). non-HDL-C abs -0.007 mmol/L derived from -0.2% x baseline 128 mg/dL. TG absolute change not reported. Events = 572+560 primary events at futility stop (~75% of 1304 planned at interim). PPARA target genetics not established -> uncertain.

LDL-C abs -0.85 mmol/L = ITT average at study midpoint (S1, ~2/3 compliance); pct -30 from Merck topline S2 (FDA-label release says 32%). Events = 526 + 619 major atherosclerotic events (key outcome). alpha 0.01 = value used in the design power calculation (on the original major-vascular-events outcome); final threshold not found. Rate ratio (log-rank) used as observed_hr. No apoB/non-HDL-C/Lp(a) changes reported.

Placebo-adjusted 12-month changes from JAMA Table 4 geometric mean ratios (TG 0.82, non-HDL 0.95, apoB 0.99 NS, LDL-C 1.03, HDL-C 1.01). Absolute changes DERIVED as (GMR-1) x baseline median (TG 240 mg/dL, non-HDL 125 mg/dL, apoB 56 mg/dL, LDL-C 75 mg/dL). LDL-C (+3%) and apoB (-1%) are discordant, so the calculator should use non-HDL-C. Omega-3 has no single genetic target -> uncertain (LPL genetics support TG lowering only through apoB). Median follow-up 42.0 months. Events = 785 + 795 adjudicated (trial stopped for futility at 1384 interim events).

LDL-C: 12-month placebo-adjusted difference of medians -50%, mean difference -47 mg/dL = -1.2 mmol/L (S1). hsCRP -37% placebo-adjusted difference of medians (S1); CRP not causal by MR. apoB (-37.6%) and non-HDL-C (-40.3%, -54 mg/dL) omitted: within-arm only, not placebo-adjusted (S9). Trial stopped early for benefit at first interim analysis (393 of 520 planned events). Events = 142 + 251.

TG abs in mmol/L (-44.5 mg/dL, Hodges-Lehmann, NEJM). LDL-C and TG at 1 year (NEJM); the LDL-C difference is mostly a +10% rise in the mineral-oil placebo arm. non-HDL-C -0.41 mmol/L from Marston 2019 (consistent with FDA within-arm medians). apoB at 2 years is a DERIVED difference of within-arm medians (FDA Table 24: -2.5% vs +7.8%; -2 vs +6 mg/dL). hsCRP -0.65 mg/L (~50%) between-arm difference per FDA briefing. LDL/apoB percent ratio 0.64 -> calculator treats as discordant and uses non-HDL-C. Target genetics uncertain: no molecular target (ChEMBL mechanism unknown); TG-pathway genetics (LPL, APOC3) causal via apoB. Alpha: overall two-sided 0.05 (1-sided 0.025); final-look alpha 0.0437 after two interims. Events = 705 + 901 primary events.

Fenofibrate added to simvastatin vs simvastatin alone. Changes are DERIVED between-arm differences in within-arm change at end of study (NEJM S1): LDL-C +2.2 mg/dL (+0.057 mmol/L, n.s.), HDL-C +0.9 mg/dL (+0.023 mmol/L), TG -15.6 points from medians (-26 mg/dL). Placebo-adjusted non-HDL-C and apoB NOT FOUND, so the lipid effect is sized from LDL-C only. Intended biomarker = triglycerides (hypothesis: lower TG and raise HDL-C); PPARA genetics uncertain. Follow-up is a mean.

Active comparator: changes are atorvastatin 80 mg minus simvastatin 20-40 mg at 1 year (JAMA Table 2), not placebo-adjusted. LDL-C abs -22.9 mg/dL = -0.59 mmol/L (CTT 2010 gives -0.55). % changes derived as difference in % change from baseline. non-HDL-C fully derived (TC -28.7 minus HDL-C -1.3 = -27.4 mg/dL = -0.71 mmol/L). apoB -0.23 g/L = -23 mg/dL. Lp(a) not reported. Events = 463 + 411 primary major coronary events; follow-up = median 4.8 years.

Active comparator: changes are the 80 mg minus 10 mg atorvastatin between-arm difference, not placebo. abs_change -0.62 mmol/L is the CTT 2010 Table 1 LDL-C difference at 1 year for TNT (S6); pct_change -23.8 is derived from the reported arm means 77 vs 101 mg/dL (S1). Events = 434 + 548 first primary events. Alpha = adjusted final threshold 0.049 (nominal 0.05, two interim analyses). Follow-up = median 4.9 years. No apoB, non-HDL-C or Lp(a) data reported.

LDL-C placebo-adjusted at 3 months, derived from S1 per-arm values (-42.9% vs -1.9%; -1.1 vs -0.05 mmol/L); lipid levels converged later in the trial (time-averaged difference not reported). Events = 396 + 408 primary events (CV death, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke). Follow-up = median 3.8 years (mean 3.2). alpha 0.05 two-sided from the revised power calculation (design paper: 4.86% two-sided after interim). No apoB/non-HDL-C/Lp(a) changes reported. Note: most primary events were CV deaths, largely non-atherosclerotic in hemodialysis, so the LDL-based calculator is expected to overpredict benefit.
